title: The world of the Old Testament, 2100–539 BCE
reviewed: 2026-10-18. Each quote was copied from the linked article and is checked by npm run verify:sources.

events.title: The Third Dynasty of Ur falls
events.summary: Elamite invaders sack Ur and end its last great dynasty. Genesis names Ur as Abram's first home.

source.quote: The kingdom of Ur was destroyed around 2004 BC by an Elamite army.

events.title: Egypt's Middle Kingdom
events.summary: Egypt is reunited under Theban kings. Trade and literature flourish along the Nile.

source.quote: The Middle Kingdom lasted from approximately 2040 to 1782 or 1700 BC

events.title: The palace archives of Mari
events.summary: Thousands of clay letters survive from Mari on the Euphrates. They show the tribal world of the patriarchs' era.

source.quote: 1761 BC under the rule of Hammurabi and defeated Zimri-Lin

events.title: The Hittite kingdom rises in Anatolia
events.summary: The Hittites rule central Anatolia from Hattusa. The Bible names Hittites among the peoples of Canaan.

source.quote: an empire centered on their capital, Hattusa (around 1650 BC)

events.title: Hatshepsut rules Egypt as pharaoh
events.summary: A queen takes the full title of pharaoh. Her temple at Deir el-Bahari still stands.

source.quote: queen regnant from c. 1479 BC until c. 1458 BC

events.title: Thutmose III wins at Megiddo
events.summary: Egypt defeats a league of Canaanite kings. Canaan stays under Egyptian rule for centuries.

source.quote: It has been claimed that this was April 16, 1457 BC

events.title: The Amarna letters
events.summary: Canaanite kings write to the pharaoh for help. Several complain of raiders called the Habiru.

quote: the earliest possible date for this correspondence is the final decade of the reign of Amenhotep III, who ruled from 1388 to 1351 BC

events.title: Ramesses II reigns
events.summary: Egypt's most famous builder reigns for 66 years. Many link the Exodus story to his era.

source.quote: approximately 1279-1213 BC, aligning with Ramesses II's reign

events.title: The Merneptah Stele names Israel
events.summary: A pharaoh's victory hymn lists Israel among the peoples of Canaan. It is the oldest known mention of Israel outside the Bible.

source.quote: Merneptah's 5th year (1208 BCE)

events.title: Ugarit is destroyed
events.summary: The Canaanite port city burns and is never rebuilt. Its tablets show the worship of Baal and El.

source.quote: 1185 BC, when it was destroyed

events.title: Ramesses III fights the Sea Peoples
events.summary: Egypt drives back seafaring raiders. One group, the Peleset, settles the coast as the Philistines.

source.quote: circa 1175 BC, when the Egyptian pharaoh Ramesses III repelled a major sea invasion

events.title: The Philistines settle the southern coast
events.summary: The Philistines build five cities on Canaan's coast. They are Israel's rivals in Judges and Samuel.

events.title: The Phoenician alphabet spreads
events.summary: A short alphabet of 22 letters spreads from the Levant coast. Hebrew, Greek, and Latin letters descend from it.

source.quote: The conventional date of 1050 BC for the emergence of the Phoenician script

events.title: The fortress of Khirbet Qeiyafa
events.summary: A walled town guards the Valley of Elah. It dates to the time of Saul and David.

source.quote: Garfinkel and Ganor have dated the site to 1050-970 BCE

events.title: Hiram I rules Tyre
events.summary: The Phoenician king of Tyre trades cedar and craftsmen. The Bible makes him an ally of David and Solomon.

source.quote: His regnal years have been calculated by some as 980 to 947 BC

events.title: The Gezer calendar
events.summary: A small limestone tablet lists the farming months. It is one of the oldest Hebrew inscriptions.

source.quote: It is commonly dated to the 10th century BCE

events.title: Shoshenq I campaigns in Canaan
events.summary: The pharaoh lists the towns he conquered on a wall at Karnak. Many link him to Shishak in 1 Kings 14.

source.quote: Shoshenq's 925 BC campaign

events.title: The Neo-Assyrian Empire rises
events.summary: Assyria builds the largest empire yet seen. Its kings will conquer Israel and besiege Jerusalem.

source.quote: Beginning with the accession of Adad-nirari II in 911 BCE

events.title: Ahab fights Assyria at Qarqar
events.summary: A league of kings meets Shalmaneser III in Syria. Assyrian records say Ahab brought 2,000 chariots.

source.quote: The Battle of Qarqar (or Ḳarḳar) was fought in 853 BC

events.title: King Mesha of Moab raises his stele
events.summary: Mesha boasts of throwing off Israel's rule. 2 Kings 3 tells the same revolt from Israel's side.

source.quote: a stele dated around 840 BCE

events.title: The Tel Dan stele names the house of David
events.summary: An Aramean king boasts of killing two kings. One belonged to the house of David.

source.quote: an important regional figure in the late 9th century BCE

events.title: Jehu bows on the Black Obelisk
events.summary: Shalmaneser III records the tribute of Jehu of Israel. It is the only known picture of a king of Israel.

quote: The stele describes how Jehu brought or sent his tribute in or around 841 BC.
erected as a public monument in 825 BC

events.title: Tiglath-Pileser III expands Assyria
events.summary: The king called Pul in the Bible takes tribute from Israel. He deports whole peoples to hold his empire.

source.quote: numerous officials and governors were replaced after 745

events.title: Sargon II completes the fall of Samaria
events.summary: Sargon claims to have carried off 27,290 people of Samaria. He builds a new capital at Khorsabad.

source.quote: the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 722 BC to his death in battle in 705

events.title: Taharqa of Kush rules Egypt
events.summary: A Kushite pharaoh rules from the Nile to the Delta. 2 Kings 19 names him Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia.

source.quote: Taharqa's reign can be dated from 690 BC to 664 BC.

events.title: Hezekiah's tunnel and the Siloam inscription
events.summary: Diggers cut a tunnel through rock to bring spring water inside Jerusalem. An inscription tells how the two crews met.

source.quote: dated to the 8th century BC on the basis of the writing style

events.title: Sennacherib's prisms tell of Hezekiah
events.summary: Clay prisms record the campaign of 701 BCE. They say Hezekiah was shut up in Jerusalem like a caged bird.

source.quote: They were created during the reign of Sennacherib in 689 BC (Chicago) or 691 BC (London, Jerusalem).

events.title: The siege of Lachish is carved at Nineveh
events.summary: Assyria storms Judah's second city. Sennacherib's palace walls show the siege in carved stone.

source.quote: during the siege of Lachish in 701 BC

events.title: Esarhaddon conquers Egypt
events.summary: Sennacherib's son takes Memphis from Taharqa. Assyria reaches its greatest extent.

source.quote: his conquest of Egypt in 671 BC

events.title: Psamtik I frees Egypt from Assyria
events.summary: A king from Sais reunites Egypt. His dynasty fights Babylon in Jeremiah's day.

source.quote: between 664 and 610 BCE

events.title: Lydia strikes the first coins
events.summary: The kingdom of Lydia stamps lumps of electrum with a mark of value. Coinage spreads across the Greek world.

source.quote: Lydian coins, made of electrum, are among the oldest in existence, dated to around the 7th century BC.

events.title: The silver scrolls of Ketef Hinnom
events.summary: Two tiny silver amulets carry the priestly blessing of Numbers 6. They are the oldest known Bible text.

source.quote: dated paleographically to the late 7th or early 6th century BCE

events.title: Josiah dies fighting Necho at Megiddo
events.summary: Pharaoh Necho II marches north to help Assyria. King Josiah of Judah tries to stop him and is killed.

source.quote: This Battle of Megiddo is recorded as having taken place in 609 BC

events.title: Babylon defeats Egypt at Carchemish
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar routs Necho's army on the Euphrates. Judah passes from Egypt's sway to Babylon's.

source.quote: The armies of Necho II and Nebuchadnezzar II met at or near Carchemish in 605 BCE.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar II rules Babylon
events.summary: Babylon's greatest king takes Jerusalem twice and rebuilds his capital in glazed brick.

source.quote: ruling from the death of his father Nabopolassar in 605 BC to his own death in 562 BC

events.title: A Babylonian chronicle records Jerusalem's capture
events.summary: A clay tablet says Nebuchadnezzar seized the city of Judah and appointed a new king. 2 Kings 24 tells the same events.

source.quote: establish that Nebuchadnezzar captured Jerusalem the first time on March 16, 597 BC

events.title: Babylon feeds the captive king Jehoiachin
events.summary: Palace ration lists name Jehoiachin, king of Judah, and his sons. 2 Kings 25 ends with his release.

source.quote: Jehoiachin's rations tablets date from the 6th century BC

events.title: Pharaoh Apries, the Hophra of Jeremiah
events.summary: Apries sends an army to relieve besieged Jerusalem but fails. Jeremiah 44 names him Pharaoh Hophra.

source.quote: a pharaoh of Egypt (589-570 BCE)

events.title: The Lachish letters
events.summary: Officers at Lachish write on potsherds as Babylon closes in. Jeremiah 34 names Lachish among the last cities standing.

source.quote: shortly before Lachish fell to the Babylonian army of King Nebuchadnezzar II in 588/6 BC

events.title: The Ishtar Gate of Babylon
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar builds a blue glazed gate with dragons and bulls. Judah's exiles would have known it.

source.quote: 569 BC by order of King Nebuchadnezzar II

events.title: Nabonidus leaves Belshazzar in charge of Babylon
events.summary: Babylon's last king spends years at an Arabian oasis. His son Belshazzar governs, as in Daniel 5.

source.quote: ruling from 556 BC to the fall of Babylon

events.title: Cyrus takes Babylon
events.summary: Persian forces enter Babylon and end its empire. The Jewish exiles soon receive leave to go home.

source.quote: The fall of Babylon occurred in 539 BCE

events.title: The Cyrus Cylinder
events.summary: Cyrus records that he let deported peoples return home with their gods. Ezra 1 gives his decree for the Jews.

source.quote: The British Museum puts the Cylinder's date of origin at between 539 and 530 BC.

events.title: The kingdom of Saba in Arabia
events.summary: Sabaeans grow rich on the incense trade from southern Arabia. Many link them to the Queen of Sheba.

source.quote: The first Sabaean kingdom lasted from the 8th century BCE to the 1st century BCE
